title: Agent-assisted SGLang development: an initial exploration
gist: SGLang packaged benchmarking, profiling, CUDA debugging and incident triage as skills agents can run, and set up a loop in which one coding agent implements, another reviews, and a profile must explain a gap before any patch is written. A November recap says agents now produce most of the project's merged pull requests.
changes: The second open engine to say in public that agents do the bulk of its engineering. Its own example of a kernel win evaporating end to end is the cleanest small illustration of the evaluation problem.
caveats: The recap's claims (most merged pull requests, decoding up to 2x faster from AI-written megakernels, a port to a new accelerator in under a week) come without percentages, hardware or model. The post itself warns about plausible-but-wrong changes and reward hacking through mismatched ABI or fast-math flags.

numbers.metric: A kernel-group speed-up measured end to end
numbers.baseline: the same change measured in isolation

bears_on.note: Merged, public pull requests from an agent loop with a review step.
A 2x kernel win was worth 2% in the engine.
The open engines are running the loop themselves.
